newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - EMU raises questions on future BCI levels.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - EMU raises questions on future BCI levels.

text.p: Italy's BCI index may be hindered in its anticipated upward rise if the country fails to meet the joining requirements for European economic and monetary union (EMU), a Reuters survey of world stock index forecasts shows.
Eight analysts in the survey, which was carried out last week, gave a mean forecast for the BCI of 791.9 for end-1997, compared with the market close of 763.44 on March 11.
Three analysts gave predictions for 1998, ranging from 810 to 900, the upper limit of which would bring the Italian market close to its all-time closing high of 908.2 recorded on 20 May 1986.

Market sentiment is not that optimistic. The Europe problem is having an effect on Btp futures and on Italy's credibility. There are still hopes we will join the single currency but if these are not fulfilled, the bourse index will fall below 720.

The interest rate outlook remains good. There are still uncertainties over the single European currency. The scenario is certainly better than three months ago. The Italian equities market saw a huge inflow of liquidity at the beginning of 1997 as investors switched interest into stocks and out of lower-yielding Italian government bonds.

Aside from the positive scenario on interest rates, I don't see the bourse expecting strong company profits. There are still a lot of problems linked to the need for privatisation which do not encourage excessive optimism.
